ai_disclosure: AI was used to read the regulation text into rule candidates. Values labeled 'Derived' come from readings that passed review; values labeled 'Interpretation' come from readings not yet reviewed, or depend on a condition the engine does not model. In this demo that review was an AI review applied on the project owner's instruction, not a person's; each value's source panel says which. No AI model is used to compute this assessment.

items.explanation: Lot is 60 ft wide (50 ft or more): 5.0 ft for a building up to two stories and 18 ft. Any floor or portion of a floor with a ceiling height greater than 14 feet shall count as twice the square footage of that area.

(1) Said parking is located within the rear half of the Lot, or at least 55 feet from a Front Lot Line.
(2) On a Through Lot with no Rear Lot Line, said parking is set back from both Front Lot Lines a distance of at least 40 feet.

items.explanation: 0.45 x lot area (8,100 sq ft), for a lot outside the Hillside Area and Coastal Zone. The encroachment plane that starts 20 ft above the front and side yards is not drawn. What counts (LAMC 12.03): area under a ceiling over 14 ft counts twice; required covered parking is not counted up to 400 sq ft when all of it is in the rear half or at least 55 ft from the front (otherwise 200 sq ft), nor detached accessory buildings of 200 sq ft or less, up to 400 sq ft in all. Lattice-roof porches and qualifying basements are not counted either.

items.explanation: Allowed as an accessory use only on a lot of at least 10,000 sq ft; this lot is 8,100 sq ft. Accessory living quarters are for guests only: no kitchen, not rented, at most two stories, and they count toward the lot's floor area (LAMC 12.03, LAMC 12.08 A.7). With a kitchen or for rent it is an ADU instead (see below).

items.explanation: The lot is within half a mile, in a straight line, of a major transit stop or high-quality transit corridor in Caltrans' layer (a frequent bus corridor). State law allows 18 ft within half a mile walking distance, plus 2 ft for a roof pitch that matches the house, so up to 20 ft. items.explanation: Up to 2 homes on the lot, approved ministerially (Gov. Code 65852.21(a)). Local standards may not prevent two units of at least 800 sq ft each, and side and rear setbacks may be at most 4 ft (none for an existing structure rebuilt in place) (65852.21(b)). Checked: the lot is in a single-family zone (R1); no historic preservation overlay (HPOZ) is mapped here. The loaded maps show no Very High fire hazard zone, earthquake fault zone or 100-year flood plain here (Gov. Code 65913.4(a)(6)(D), (F) and (G)). Still to confirm: no demolition or alteration of rent-restricted or rent-controlled housing, or housing a tenant occupied in the last 3 years; no units withdrawn from rent under the Ellis Act in the last 15 years; the Gov. Code 65913.4(a)(6) sites not mapped here: farmland (B), wetlands (C), listed hazardous waste sites (E), a regulatory floodway (H), natural community conservation plan lands (I), protected species habitat (J) and conservation easements (K). SB 9 uses that section as it read on 2021-09-16; the copy loaded here is the 2026 text, whose (B)-(K) list the same kinds of site.
